summary: FireSI is an interactive, Super Intelligence (SI)-powered web platform designed to analyze microgravity combustion data and enhance spacecraft fire safety. Addressing the "Flame in Freefall" challenge, our application transforms complex, raw experimental datasets from NASA's Physical Science Informatics (PSI) Data Repository and historical spaceflight records into actionable safety insights. Unlike on Earth, fire in microgravity behaves unpredictably due to the absence of buoyancy-driven convection, posing severe risks to astronauts and missions. FireSI features a Mission Overview dashboard, an interactive Investigation Explorer, real-time data quality analytics, and SI-driven risk modeling to detect hidden combustion anomalies, flame spread patterns, and ignition thresholds. By making open microgravity fire research accessible and predictive, FireSI empowers mission planners, aerospace engineers, and researchers to design safer habitats, select flame-resistant materials, and prevent catastrophic fire hazards during long-duration lunar and Martian space exploration.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

FireSI (Fire Safety Intelligence) is a full-stack analytical web application built to bridge the gap between raw microgravity combustion experiments and practical spacecraft fire-prevention protocols. The platform ingests structured datasets from NASA’s Physical Science Informatics (PSI) Data Repository alongside historical spaceflight records from the Apollo 1 (AS-204) and Apollo 13 missions, processing them through a real-time data pipeline. Users can navigate through three core modules:

1. Mission Overview: Visualizes key combustion metrics, historical spaceflight fire and environmental safety lessons (including Apollo 1 and Apollo 13), and mission risk indicators.

2. Investigation Explorer: Allows researchers and engineers to filter, compare, and inspect microgravity flame behavior, fuel flammability limits, and smoke/gas emissions across different gravity levels and atmospheric compositions.

3. Data Quality & SI Insights: Evaluates dataset integrity and applies Super Intelligence (SI) pattern recognition to highlight critical ignition triggers and flame-spread anomalies that are invisible in standard Earth-based tests.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

Fire is one of the most dangerous emergencies aboard a crewed spacecraft. By translating dense scientific tables into an intuitive, visual decision-support tool, FireSI reduces the time engineers spend manually cross-referencing combustion studies. Its intended impact is to directly support safer spacecraft cabin material selection, improved fire detection sensor placement, and stronger emergency suppression protocols for the International Space Station (ISS), Artemis lunar habitats, and future Mars missions.

Tools, Languages & Architecture Used:

- Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite, and Tailwind CSS for a fast, responsive, and accessible user interface.

- Backend & Real-Time Engine: Node.js / TypeScript backend with real-time subscriber modules for live telemetry and dataset querying.

- Data & Visualization: Structured CSV/JSON research pipelines and custom SVG architectural and analytical diagrams.

USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE / SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI)

💻 AI/SI tools & software used:

• Gemini

• ChatGPT

• GitHub Copilot

• Nano Banana

Creativity & Key Factors Considered:

Rather than presenting static scientific charts, we designed FireSI as a mission-control-style research assistant. In building the platform, our team carefully considered accessibility (clean visual hierarchy and readable telemetry dashboards for both scientists and students), computational efficiency (lightweight client-side rendering via Vite), and scientific validity by grounding every insight directly in verified NASA microgravity datasets and Apollo mission safety benchmarks.
